results.title: Optical Coherence Tomography and Coherence Domain ...
results.content: Directions of research and development in areas such as optical coherence tomography (OCT), low-coherence interferometry, speckle-based measurement and imaging technologies, coherent light microscopy, and coherence technologies for novel-contrast imaging including flow, polarization and intrinsic tissue functional imaging will be considered. Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) offers high-speed, non-invasive deep tissue imaging, but speckle noise degrades image quality by obscuring true structures and limiting resolution. Phase retardation measured by polarization-sensitive optical coherence tomography (PS-OCT) depends on the tissue angle relative to the imaging beam. OCT-signal-model-based single-image speckle reduction for high-resolution and high-contrast imaging of full-field swept-source optical coherence tomography. We propose a numerical speckle reduction method for full-field swept-source optical coherence tomography (FF-SSOCT), which is based on an analytic signal formation model of OCT and used only one complex OCT image. We developed a wide-field, non-contact, multimodal visible-light optical coherence tomography (vis-OCT) and scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (SLO) system for mouse retinal imaging, enabling the visualization of peripheral retinal structure, vasculature, and fluorescently labeled microglia.

results.title: Optical Elastography and Tissue Biomechanics XIII
results.content: The emerging field of optical elastography uses optics to characterize tissues and cells based on their elastic and viscoelastic mechanical properties, complementing related biomechanics methods such as atomic force microscopy, traction force microscopy, microrheology, ultrasound, and magnetic resonance elastography. This conference aims to bring together technology and applications experts in bioengineering, biophysics, cell biology, clinical sciences, medical imaging, optical microscopy, optics and photonics, and tissue engineering to foster interdisciplinary connections and advance the field of tissue biomechanics. Papers are solicited on biomedical optics, biophotonics, a combination of optical methods with ultrasound and MRI elastography, and biomechanical methods and technologies applied or related to estimation, monitoring, and functional assessment of the mechanical properties of normal and pathological biomaterials at all spatial scales, from cells and their constituents to tissues and organs. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) offers high-resolution tissue imaging, and optical coherence elastography (OCE) shows promise for cancer detection.
